Subject: Regional evacuation action plan — immediate steps for service continuity (US/EU)

Sophie / Acme ops team —

We’re reaching out because we detected an escalating infrastructure fault affecting our US-East (us-east-1) and a subset of EU-West (eu-west-1) host pools. Engineers have identified persistent peering instability with the cloud provider for those specific zones; impact is intermittent failures and elevated latencies for requests routed to those regions.

Short version / action required from Acme: please opt your account into our temporary regional fallback so traffic serving your tenants will be routed to US-West (us-west-2) and EU-Central (eu-central-1) while we complete full remediation. This is a quick config flip on your side and should be low risk.

Why this matters: your active inference jobs that are pinned to us-east or eu-west may see errors if they cannot reach our replicas in those zones. The fallback will keep sessions alive and maintain throughput while slightly changing p95 latency characteristics. We’ll continue routing at the tenant level and preserve KV cache where possible.

Immediate steps (we attached a one-page checklist — regional_reroute_checklist.pdf):
1) Add the following fallback parameter to your API client config (one-line change):

  // example (pseudocode)
  redwood.setRoutingPolicy({
    preferred_region: "us-east-1,eu-west-1",
    fallback_order: ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"],
    region_fallback_enabled: true
  });

2) If you use IP allowlists, add these temporary egress ranges: 34.200.12.0/24, 52.17.33.0/24. (Full CIDR list in checklist.)
3) Set a 2-minute retry on transient 5xx responses.
4) Confirm back on this thread with the timestamp you plan to flip (we suggest within the next 60–90 minutes to avoid queued requests).

What Redwood will do:
- Execute automatic traffic steering for any requests we still see arriving for us-east/eu-west.
- Perform smoke tests once you opt in and send a validation note.
- Provide a post-incident summary and one-time service credit for impacted token usage.

Attachments: regional_reroute_checklist.pdf, traffic-shift-diagram.png

I’ll coordinate internal ops and keep this thread as the single source of truth. If you prefer a short call, I’m available for a 15-minute bridge immediately.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

Subject: Follow-up: Post-incident summary and next steps (Acme Advertising)

Sophie / Acme ops —

Thanks again for working through the fallback today. Recap and next steps below; please consider this the official post-incident note while we finalize the public postmortem.

Timeline recap (UTC):
- 2026-12-12T07:00Z: Initial peering instability detected (us-east / eu-west host pools).
- 2026-12-12T07:14Z: Customer notifications issued and fallback guidance shared.
- 2026-12-12T07:45Z: Acme enabled regional_fallback; Redwood began traffic steering.
- 2026-12-12T07:50Z: Smoke tests executed by Redwood operations (passed for generation/chat/embeddings routes).
- 2026-12-12T08:20Z: Primary provider confirmed partial routing restoration; gradual healing to follow.

Observed impact for Acme: a brief window of elevated 5xxs and increased p95 latency while traffic moved to fallback regions. We validated response quality and saw no data loss.

Compensation: Ben approved a one-time service credit up to $1,200 (we’ll post the exact credit after final usage review).

What we’ve attached / links:
- regional_reroute_checklist.pdf (what we asked customers to apply)
- traffic-shift-diagram.png (visual of routing change)
- postmortem-draft.md (internal draft; we will publish a redacted version to customers by EOD Monday)
- Incident page: https://redwood.statuspage.io/incidents/rdw-2026-12-11

Operational asks for Acme (non-blocking):
- If you can, please confirm the allowlist changes were applied successfully and if you saw any blocked egress logs.
- We recommend leaving region_fallback_enabled for 24 hours to ensure session stability; you can revert after that window if you prefer.

We’ll schedule a short review next week to go over the final postmortem and any follow-up action items for longer-term routing resiliency. Thanks for your patience — and apologies for the disruption.

Best,
